config.title: Where to Eat Near Museum Island - FAQ
config.subtitle: Cafés on the island, the Monday and Tuesday closures, and the restaurants a short walk from each museum exit.

items.q: Are there restaurants on Museum Island?
items.a: Only inside the buildings. Every museum has a small café, and **Cu29** in the James-Simon-Galerie is a café and restaurant with a terrace above the Kupfergraben, open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00. You can walk into the James-Simon-Galerie without a museum ticket.

items.q: Where can I eat near Museum Island on a Monday?
items.a: The island museums and their cafés are closed on Mondays. Walk five minutes south to the **Humboldt Forum**: the **Lebenswelten Bistro** on the ground floor is open every day and free to enter, and the rooftop **Restaurant Baret** opens from 11:00.
The Humboldt Forum exhibitions and **Restaurant Baret** on its roof. The island museums, Cu29 and the museum cafés are open, and the Lebenswelten Bistro stays open too.

items.q: Where is the closest sit-down lunch to the Bode-Museum?
items.a: **Deponie Nr. 3** in the S-Bahn arches on Georgenstraße, about five minutes on foot across the Kupfergraben. It serves Berlin food daily from 10:00 and takes German debit cards or cash, not credit cards. Hackescher Markt is about ten minutes away through Monbijou Park.

items.q: Can I leave Museum Island for lunch and come back?
items.a: Yes. The **Museum Island day ticket (EUR 24)** covers every open museum on the island for that day, so you can eat off the island and visit a second museum afterwards.

items.q: Which riverside restaurant is near Museum Island?
items.a: **Brauhaus Georgbräu** at Spreeufer 4 in the Nikolaiviertel, opposite the Humboldt Forum. It brews its own beer, opens daily from 12:00 and has a beer garden on the Spree. Plan at least an hour.
